extracted.intended_audience: vehicle manufacturers, compliance engineers, legal counsel, and members of the public interested in commenting on NHTSA petitions
extracted.subtask_description: Notice of receipt of a manufacturer's petition requesting that NHTSA find certain regulatory noncompliances to be inconsequential to motor vehicle safety and exempt the manufacturer from notification and remedy duties. Includes statutory basis, the FMVSS provisions at issue, the manufacturer's supporting arguments, and public comment procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory basis for petition/exemption (49 U.S.C. 30118(d), 30120(h); 49 CFR part 556)
rubrics_metrics.description: Petition filed pursuant to 49 U.S.C. 30118(d) and 30120(h) and 49 CFR part 556 requesting an exemption from the notification and remedy requirements on the basis that the noncompliance is inconsequential as it relates to motor vehicle safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any decision on such a petition only exempts manufacturers from the duties in sections 30118 and 30120 to notify owners, purchasers, and dealers and to remedy the noncompliance; it applies only to vehicles the manufacturer no longer controls at the time the noncompliance was determined. A grant does not relieve vehicle distributors and dealers of prohibitions on sale/offer for sale or introduction into interstate commerce of noncompliant vehicles under their control after notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noncompliance reporting requirement (49 CFR part 573)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manufacturers must file a noncompliance report pursuant to 49 CFR part 573 when they determine a vehicle does not comply with an applicable FMVSS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice references Ford's noncompliance report dated June 9, 2023. Filing the report is a prerequisite and contextual fact for later filing of an inconsequentiality petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: FMVSS No. 138 — Paragraph S4.5(a) owner's manual content requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraph S4.5(a) of FMVSS No. 138 requires that the owner's manual provided with each vehicle certified as complying with paragraph S4 must include the statement specified in paragraph S4.5(a), which details the importance of maintaining proper tire pressure and explains the functionality of the tire pressure monitoring system (TPMS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the required TPMS statement is missing from printed materials, a petition must explain where and how the required statement is otherwise available to the vehicle owner (e.g., in a DOM, online manual, or mobile app).

rubrics_metrics.name: FMVSS No. 209 — Paragraph S4.1(l) seat belt written instructions requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraph S4.1(l) of FMVSS No. 209 requires that a seat belt assembly include written instructions on the proper use, maintenance and periodic inspection of the seatbelt assembly and related components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition arguing inconsequentiality should identify whether the required written instructions were provided in the owner's manual, supplemental printed documents, or by alternative means (digital/manual) and provide supporting detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format requirement for providing required information (NHTSA Chief Counsel 2009 interpretation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain FMVSSs require information to be provided in written form, either in owner's manuals if one is provided, or in a paper format, per a May 18, 2009 interpretation by NHTSA's Chief Counsel's Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NHTSA has noted advantages of hard copy manuals and historically has not adopted a compliance option permitting digital manuals in lieu of printed copies; petitions relying on digital delivery should address this precedent and show why digital provision is functionally equivalent or otherwise supports inconsequentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument/evidence: availability of required information via integrated digital owner's manual (DOM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manufacturer's contention that required owner's manual content, though missing from the printed Supplemental Owner's Guide (SOG), is available to customers in the Digital Owner's Manual (DOM) displayed on the vehicle's center console infotainment screen and online/mobile platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition should show how the DOM is organized (table of contents, search function), how it is accessed (Appendix steps), and argue why these features make the information as available and usable as printed material (e.g., integrated in-vehicle, cannot be misplaced).

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument/evidence: availability of required information via online/manual/mobile apps
rubrics_metrics.description: Manufacturer's assertion that owner's manual content is publicly available at ford.com/support and lincoln.com/support, and accessible through 'Ford Pass' and 'Lincoln Way' mobile applications, including by VIN or model/year lookup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions should detail access steps (appendices), mention any app/registration/internet connectivity requirements, and explain how online/mobile availability provides the required written information to vehicle owners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument/evidence: field performance and lack of reported incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: Manufacturer's search of internal records and Vehicle Owner Questionnaires (VOQs) finding no evidence of customers experiencing confusion or lacking information regarding TPMS indicators or seatbelt maintenance and no related complaints, accidents, or injuries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While absence of complaints is not dispositive, petitions commonly present such evidence to illustrate that the noncompliance has not resulted in safety-related incidents; provide search methodology, timeframes, and any contextual limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument/evidence: remedial/corrective actions taken
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentation of corrective actions — e.g., OTA software updates that unintentionally deleted and later restored the DOM for many vehicles, and a field service action plus mailed owner's manuals for remaining affected units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show steps taken to restore access or otherwise mitigate any lack of printed content; such remedial steps can support a claim of inconsequentiality or demonstrate low safety risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precedent and comparative petitions (use of prior decisions/filings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Citation of prior petitions or agency interpretations (e.g., Maserati North America, Inc. 2020 petition and NHTSA 2009 letters) as supportive precedent for arguments about digital/manual formats and inconsequentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions commonly cite prior petitions and NHTSA interpretations; include citations, factual parallels, and distinctions to strengthen the legal argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope/limits of any grant (effect on dealers and distributors)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition decision allowing inconsequentiality exemptions applies only to duties under 49 U.S.C. 30118 and 30120 for vehicles no longer controlled by the manufacturer; it does not relieve vehicle distributors and dealers of prohibitions on sale or introduction into interstate commerce of noncompliant vehicles under their control after notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners should be aware that an agency grant is narrowly tailored and does not provide broader relief for parties other than the manufacturer for vehicles still under their control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice vs. decision — publication and administrative effect
rubrics_metrics.description: This Federal Register notice of receipt announces only that NHTSA has received a petition; it 'does not represent any agency decision or another exercise of judgment concerning the merits of the petition.' When the petition is granted or denied, notice of the decision will be published in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders should treat the notice as procedural and submit comments if they wish to affect the ultimate agency decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment submission procedures and formal requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested persons invited to submit written data, views, and arguments by the specified closing date; comments must refer to the docket and notice number and may be submitted by mail, hand delivery, electronically at regulations.gov, or by fax. Comments must be in English and be no greater than 15 pages in length (attachments unlimited). If submitted in hard copy, provide two copies. Include instructions for requesting confirmation of receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the stated methods and formatting: include docket/notice number, adhere to the 15-page limit for the comment body, understand attachments may be longer, provide two hard copies if mailing, and use a stamped self-addressed postcard to request receipt confirmation. Late submissions will be filed and considered to the fullest extent possible but timely submission is preferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public posting and confidentiality considerations for comments
rubrics_metrics.description: All comments received will be posted without change to regulations.gov, including any personal information provided. Agencies may choose to redact or withhold certain submissions (or portions thereof).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters should avoid including unnecessary personal information if privacy is a concern and may request redaction per agency procedures; assume comments become public record unless redaction/withholding is approved by the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and authority of official documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal Register prototype on federalregister.gov is informational; use the PDF linked to govinfo.gov for the official electronic format. Only official editions of the Federal Register provide legal notice and judicial notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relying on the notice for legal or procedural purposes, verify content against the official PDF on govinfo.gov and consult the Document Drafting Handbook or official sources for drafting details or authoritative text.
